Synthetic: head of household, wages $120,000, one qualifying child age 10 with an SSN; foreign tax $25 by election. The child tax credit is $2,200 and the tax exceeds it, so line 14 takes line 12 and no additional credit arises. Predicted by the authoring session from the archived Schedule 8812 and i1040gi pp. 14, 17-19; no independent human hand-work is claimed.  Shown-line regression (owner decision 2026-10-26: skipped lines are hidden): line 16a is zero, so f1040s8812 line 16a "If zero, stop here" hides lines 16b to 26.

Synthetic: head of household, wages $4,000, one qualifying child age 3. No tax, so the whole $2,200 is unused (line 16a); line 16b is $1,700; earned income $4,000 less $2,500 at 15% gives $225 on line 20; fewer than three children, so Part II-B is skipped and line 27 is the smaller of line 17 ($1,700) and line 20 ($225). The Part II-B lines are still computed: withheld social security $248 plus Medicare $58 is $306 on lines 21, 23 and 25, which exceeds line 20, so line 26 is $306. Predicted by the authoring session from the archived Schedule 8812; no independent human hand-work is claimed. Stage 9: the EIC applies (one qualifying child with a valid SSN, head of household, earned income and AGI $4,000); predicted by hand from the printed EIC Table row $4,000-$4,050, one child, $1,369 (i1040gi p. 50), Worksheet A line 4 Yes so line 6 is line 2; the refund rises by $1,369; Part II-B line 24 carries the EIC.  Shown-line regression (owner decision 2026-10-26: skipped lines are hidden): line 16b is under $5,100 and not Puerto Rico, so the Next instruction after line 20 skips Part II-B.

Synthetic: head of household, wages $30,000, three qualifying children (ages 2, 5, 8). Line 8 is $6,600; the tax is $638 (taxable income $6,375 after the $23,625 head of household standard deduction, read from the Tax Table, whose cell is the rounded tax at the midpoint of the $6,350-$6,400 row), so line 14 is $638 and line 16a is $5,962; line 16b is exactly $5,100, which is "$5,100 or more", so Part II-B applies; line 20 ($4,125) is less than line 17 ($5,100); withheld social security and Medicare total $2,295 on line 25; line 26 is the larger, $4,125; line 27 is the smaller of line 17 and line 26, $4,125. Predicted by the authoring session from the archived Schedule 8812; no independent human hand-work is claimed. Stage 9: the EIC applies; printed row $30,000-$30,050, three children, $6,640 (i1040gi p. 53); line 4 Yes; Part II-B line 25 falls to zero and line 26 stays at line 20, so the ACTC is unchanged and the refund rises by $6,640.

Synthetic: head of household, wages $5,000, three qualifying children. No tax; line 16a $6,600; line 16b $5,100; line 20 is 15% of $2,500, $375; withheld social security $310 plus Medicare $72.50 is $382.50 on line 25, which is larger than line 20, so line 26 is $382.50 and line 27 is the smaller of line 17 ($5,100) and line 26, $382.50. Predicted by the authoring session from the archived Schedule 8812; no independent human hand-work is claimed. Stage 9: the EIC applies; printed row $5,000-$5,050, three children, $2,261 (i1040gi p. 50); Part II-B line 25 ($382.50 before) falls to zero once line 24 carries the EIC, so line 26 is line 20 ($375) and the ACTC falls by $7.50; refund $882.50 - $7.50 + $2,261 = $3,136. Shown state (T-232, predicted from the form before evaluating): line 16b is $5,100 and line 20 ($375) is less than line 17 ($5,100), so Part II-B is completed (f1040s8812 after line 20, "On line 16b, is the amount $5,100 or more? ... The three-child head of household return of stage8.hoh.actc.three_children with wages of $340,000 and nontaxable combat pay reported. Line 8 is $6,600; line 9 $200,000; line 10 $140,000; line 11 5% = $7,000. Line 12: 'Is the amount on line 8 more than the amount on line 11? ... No. Stop here. You cannot take the child tax credit, credit for other dependents, or additional child tax credit.' So line 12 is $0 and line 27 (the ACTC) is $0, with Form 1040 line 28 $0; Part II-A, where the combat pay would be entered (Earned Income Worksheet line 1b), is not reached.

Stage 9, predicted by hand from the printed instructions before recording: Single, one child, wages $120,000, nontaxable combat pay: AGI is above every EIC limit, so line 27a is $0 and Schedule 8812 line 18a comes from the Earned Income Worksheet, whose line 1b refuses for combat pay (i1040s8812 p. 7, Earned Income Chart).

cases.evidence_note: Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (Schedule 1 line 8, Schedule A, the Tax Table, the EIC), i1040sca, i1040s8812 and p525, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding and agreed on every shared value; recorded after comparison. Facts: Head of household with one qualifying child aged 6. Wages $20,000. Gambling winnings $5,000; no losses. Working (predictor A): s1 8b 5,000; 9 5,000; 10 5,000. AGI 25,000; HOH standard 23,625; 15 = 1,375; Tax Table HOH 1,375-1,400 = 139; 18 = 139. EIC (i1040gi EIC Worksheet A, one child): line 1 earned income 20,000 -> table 4,328 (line 2); line 3 AGI 25,000 is not less than 23,350, so line 5 looks up 25,000-25,050 -> 4,060 (check: 4,328 - 15.98% x (25,025 - 23,350) = 4,060.33); line 6 smaller = 4,060 -> f1040 27a. Gambling winnings are not investment income for the EIC test (interest, dividends, capital gains, rents/royalties, passive). Schedule 8812: 1/3 = 25,000; 4 = 1; 5 = 2,200; 8 = 2,200; 9 = 200,000; 10 = 0; 11 = 0; 12 = 2,200; Credit Limit Worksheet A line 1 = f1040 18 = 139, line 2 = 0 (no Schedule 3 credits), 3 = 139, 5 = 139 -> 13 = 139; 14 = smaller(2,200, 139) = 139. 16a = 2,061; 16b = 1 x 1,700 = 1,700; 17 = 1,700; 18a = 20,000; 19 = 17,500; 20 = 2,625; 16b < 5,100 so 27 = smaller(17, 20) = 1,700.

Mutation scenario for Credit Limit Worksheet B lines 7 to 12 (T-051). Two agents worked the return by hand from the archived f1040, i1040gi, f1040s1, f1040sse, f8995, i8995, f1040s8812, i1040s8812 (Credit Limit Worksheets A and B, the Earned Income Chart and Worksheet), f5695 and i5695 without the encoding and agreed on every asserted value but one, Residential Clean Energy Credit Limit Worksheet line 2, which i5695 p. 5 (its footnote) sets to Credit Limit Worksheet B line 14 when that worksheet is completed, as stage15.f5695-2.e12 records; the expected values are theirs. Lines after a skip are not asserted. Facts: head of household, unmarried, age 40; solar electric property $5,000 on the existing main home; taxable interest $15,000 (over the $11,950 investment income limit, so no EIC); nothing else. Three qualifying children aged 3, 6 and 9. One W-2: boxes 1, 3 and 5 $1,000, box 4 $62.00, box 6 $14.50. A sole proprietorship with $2,000 of gross receipts and no expenses (Schedule SE line 12 $282.59; half, $141.295, entered as $141.30).
